title: Worksheet — Timeline and Sources of History (Class 6 CBSE Social Science)
instructions: Attempt all 11 questions. Show your working where required. Total time: 50 minutes.

questions.question: There is no year zero in the BCE/CE system.
Indian history is broadly divided into:
How many years passed between 1500 BCE and 500 CE? Show working.
questions.answer: 1500 + 500 − 1 = 1999 years (subtract 1 because there is no year zero).

questions.question: Place the following events in the right broad period (Ancient / Medieval / Modern): Harappan civilisation, British rule, Cholas, Mauryas.
questions.answer: Ancient: Harappan civilisation, Mauryas. Medieval: Cholas. Modern: British rule.

questions.question: Name the three families of historical sources, with one example of each.
questions.answer: (i) Archaeological — coin / pottery. (ii) Literary — Vedas / inscription. (iii) Oral — folk song / family genealogy.

questions.question: An archaeologist excavates a site and finds, from top to bottom: (i) iron tools, (ii) bronze tools, (iii) painted pottery, (iv) charcoal. (a) Order the layers from oldest to most recent. (b) Which item could be radiocarbon-dated, and why? (c) What does this tell you about the people who lived here?
questions.answer: (a) Older lies deeper, so oldest → newest: charcoal → painted pottery → bronze tools → iron tools (top). (b) Charcoal can be radiocarbon-dated because it is once-living organic material; C-14 dating only works on once-living samples. (c) The site shows a long sequence of habitation: an early people who used fire, then a culture making painted pottery, then bronze users, finally iron users — the typical Stone → Bronze → Iron progression.

questions.question: A king's inscription claims he won every battle he fought. As a historian, how would you decide whether to believe it? Discuss the questions you would ask of the source and what other evidence you would seek.
questions.answer: I would ask WHO made the inscription — the king or his official, who has reason to praise him. I would ask WHY it was made — to celebrate the king. I would ask WHAT it leaves out — defeats, taxes, hardship of subjects. I would search for INDEPENDENT sources: a rival king's inscription, a foreign traveller's diary, archaeological evidence (destroyed forts, abandoned cities, treaties), coins of rivals minted in the same area. Only if independent sources agree with the claim would I treat it as reliable history rather than royal praise.
